instructions: The night before, or at least 2 hours ahead: rinse the 1 1/2 cups jasmine rice in a sieve until the water runs mostly clear. Put it in a medium pot with 2 1/4 cups water and bring it to a boil over high heat. Cover, turn the heat to low and cook for 15 minutes. Take it off the heat and leave it covered for 10 minutes. Spread it on a plate or tray to cool, then cover and refrigerate. Cold, dry rice is what fries well, so don't use it warm.
When you're ready to cook, take the rice out of the fridge and break up any clumps with your fingers.

Cut the pork into 1/4-inch dice and toss it with 1/4 tsp of the salt. Dice the ham and the carrot the same size. Halve the shrimp lengthwise. Mince the garlic and 1 tbsp of ginger. Slice the green onions, keeping the white and green parts apart.
Beat the 3 eggs with a pinch of salt. In a small bowl, stir together 2 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp oyster sauce, the chicken broth and the white pepper.

Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in your largest wok or skillet over high heat until it shimmers. Add the pork in a single layer and leave it alone for 1 minute. Stir and cook for 2 minutes, until browned all over. Transfer it to a bowl.
You're cooking the pork to 145°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check a larger piece. No thermometer? Cut into one: it's done when it's just barely pink or white all the way through.
Add 1 tbsp oil to the pan. Add the shrimp and cook for 1 to 2 minutes, until they're pink and curled. Transfer them to the bowl with the pork.

Add 1 tbsp oil. Add the carrot and ham and stir for 2 minutes, until the ham is browned at the edges. Add the white parts of the green onions, the garlic and the ginger and stir for 20 seconds, until fragrant. Transfer everything to the bowl.
Add the last 1 tbsp oil to the pan. Pour in the eggs and scramble for about 20 seconds, until half set.
Add the rice and toss it, pressing it against the pan, for 3 minutes, until it's hot and the grains look separate and dry.
Pour the sauce over the rice and toss for 1 minute, until the liquid has gone.

Return the pork, shrimp, ham and carrot to the pan along with the frozen peas, straight from the bag. Add the 1 tbsp Shaoxing wine around the edge of the pan. Toss for 1 to 2 minutes, until everything is hot.
Take the pan off the heat and stir in the green parts of the green onions.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Serve hot, straight from the pan.
advance_prep_notes: cook and chill the rice the night before
method_notes: No readable Yangzhou version had 20 or more ratings, and RecipeTin Eats (the trusted cook for Chinese) has no Yangzhou page, so this leads with 2 Food Trippers (4.67 from 9). Made With Lau and Cooks Without Borders were also read but show no rating. All three build the dish from rice, egg, pork or ham, shrimp, peas and carrot with scallion at the end; this follows the lead's browned meat and carrot, trimmed for time (no deep frying or 20 minute cornstarch soak), and adds a little chicken broth as Cooks Without Borders does. RecipeTin Eats' plain Chinese Fried Rice (4.99 from 61) informed the technique only.
